content_evals.prompt: Survey this repository's architecture for deepening opportunities.
expected_behaviors: scopes the scan from user direction or recent git hot spots before reading widely
reads CONTEXT.md and ADRs in the scanned area before proposing anything
spawns a read-only explorer sub-agent instead of walking every file in the root context
writes a single CDN-backed HTML report to the OS temp directory, never into the repository

uses module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage, and locality as the architectural nouns, never component, service, API, or boundary as synonyms — while preserving exact identifiers and CONTEXT.md terms verbatim
labels each candidate Strong, Worth exploring, or Speculative and names a top recommendation
ends by asking which candidate to explore, with no interface proposals yet
edits no production code and starts no spec-work bundle

content_evals.prompt: I pick the second candidate from the architecture report. Let's explore it.
expected_behaviors: runs grilling rounds over the candidate's design tree with recommended answers, waiting for the user between rounds
updates CONTEXT.md inline when a term is resolved, creating it lazily
offers an ADR only when the three-part test holds, including for a load-bearing rejection
offers the design-it-twice parallel pattern for alternative interfaces
ends by routing the outcome to the durable GitHub issue lifecycle or the spec-work orchestrator
does not implement the refactor or open a work bundle itself
